meta.about: Weapon attachments (docs/unreal/LOADOUT.md 3.3): the six slots, the stats an attachment may change, the ten pack parts with their rule effects and art, and the per-gun compatibility table. Adding an attachment is one entry in `attachments` plus its id in the `compatibility` rows of the guns it fits; adding a gun is one row in `compatibility`. The pack's three handguard lengths are three guns (guns.json shorty, stick, stretch), not a slot.
meta.units: effects and clamps are in web units on the gun's JSON (config.json: metres, seconds, radians, vertical degrees); a `mul` value is a plain factor. The resolver applies them before parsing (LOADOUT.md 3.7).
meta.ops: Per stat, the effects of every fitted part are combined in this order: every `set` (in slot order; the later slot wins), then the sum of every `add`, then the product of every `mul`, then every `min` (the smallest wins), then every `max`. A stat with more than one target takes only `mul`; its combined factor is clamped to `factor` and then multiplied into each target. Each target is then clamped to its own clamp, in its own unit (null = no clamp). A stat that no fitted part names is not touched at all: no op and no clamp, so a gun with no parts is its JSON unchanged.
meta.trade: Every part that is not `baseline` must make one stat better and one worse, and its trade must be balanced: B = sum of |ln f| over its better effects, W = the same over its worse effects, using only stats with trade true and mul ops (falloff.min stands for the whole falloff); MurderInc.Loadout.DataLoads fails when B / W is outside tradeBand. Presentation stats (flash, sway, adsFov, adsLook) do not count.
meta.checks: DataLoads also checks: every target's base value of every roster gun lies inside its clamp (a target the gun lacks is skipped); every compatible build of every gun resolves with falloff.end >= falloff.start (the resolver enforces end = max(end, start); start = end is a step to min) and falloff.min inside its clamp.

adsFov.note: a narrower aimed view is a trade, neither better nor worse

adsLook.note: keeps the aimed look speed in step with a narrower view; not shown as an effect

recoil.pitch.note: the camera climb, the shake and the gun's rise and push-back follow one factor, so what the player sees is what the aim does

recoil.yaw.note: a target the gun does not have (yaw on a weaving gun, weave on the NINE) is skipped

reloadTime.note: every number under rules.reload (both lengths, every mark, each element of pressCheck) times the same factor, with no per-value clamp, so the marks stay exactly marks x factor and the clip plays at 1 / factor

flash.note: presentation: no enemy sees the flash in the web rules, so it does not count in the trade check

falloff.start.note: a gun without falloff starts from start = end = Infinity, min = 1; a `min` op makes a finite falloff. Weighed through falloff.min

length.note: a longer gun pulls back from walls sooner

sway.note: presentation: the gun's look sway; the aim does not sway in the web rules

compatibility.about: Per gun and slot: `options` the player may fit, `default` the choice of a new build (null = the factory part, no effect), `required` true when the slot can never be empty (then `default` is one of `options`), `mount` the gun's mount (guns.json mounts) the part sits on, or `variant` true when the option switches the gun's base mesh. A slot a gun does not list does not exist on that gun. A listed slot is offered only when its mount is exists (or, for a variant slot, only the options whose variant is exists); see guns.json ready.
